subject: EdgeCart discovery — latency & throughput SLOs, model sizing and topology options
messages:
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@edgecart.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@edgecart.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery call

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time this morning. Below is a concise recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Highlights (what we heard)
- Primary pain: erratic latency spikes (p95 jumps from ~120ms to 600ms) under concurrent shopping cart enrichment workload; impacts checkout conversions.
- Target SLOs: p95 <= 200ms for 95% of traffic, p99 fallbacks max 800ms (hard cap). Throughput baseline ~350 req/s with 3:1 burst buffer to 1k rps.
- Model requirements: generator + short-context retrieval (up to 1.5k tokens), prefer an open 7B-13B model quantized to int8 if that meets quality bar. Few-shot prompts, KV cache persistence desired across requests per session.
- Deployment constraints: must run inside their VPC (private deployment) for PII-sensitive fields; ability to failover to hosted in adjacent region during scheduled upgrades.

Suggested topology options (high level)
1) Dedicated VPC deployment on 4x A100-equivalent nodes, multi-Zone, with autoscale policy for spike windows; prefix KV cache on local NVMe.
2) Hybrid: primary private cluster + hosted cold pool for burst capacity routed by policy (policy: latency-first until queue > 50ms then route to hosted).
3) Canary + model-variant fallbacks: quantized 7B as default, 13B on-demand for heavy-context requests; automatic rollback on quality regression.

Mutual action plan (proposal)
- By 2027-12-24: EdgeCart to share anonymized sample traces (p95/p99 buckets and sample RTTs) and infra diagram (owner: Alex).
- By 2028-01-04: Redwood to produce a sizing sketch (node counts, expected RPS per node), cost estimate, and a short canary plan (owner: Diego).
- 2028-01-11: Technical deep-dive video (90 min) with EdgeCart SRE + Redwood infra (owner: Mina).

Attachments: contract draft we referenced will be shared after sizing (placeholder).

Thanks — I captured a few tentative assumptions in the sizing ask above; we'll confirm once we see traces.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Diego — this is great, thanks for the clear write-up. A couple of clarifications and answers to your asks:

- We'll export traces with header timing and correlated request IDs; expect a ~500MB gzipped file (sanitized).
- Our checkout enrichment pipeline has a bimodal load: steady 300-400 rps with 2 x 10-minute peak windows around marketing blasts that push toward 900-1,000 rps.
- For quality, we require less than 2% fallback to general LLM for hallucination-sensitive fields (payment descriptors). If quantized 7B meets that bar in your evaluation, we'd prefer it for cost reasons.

I attached our infra sketch so you can see our current VPC layout and NAT/bastion setup. Also attaching a one-page Ops constraints doc.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeCart

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery call

Alex — perfect, thanks for the infra diagram and the workload detail. A few updates to the MAP and immediate asks from our side: 

- Action: EdgeCart to drop traces + example payloads in the Drive folder linked below by 2027-12-24 (Alex).
- Redwood will run a short synthetic sizing simulation against a replayed sample (non-production) to validate node counts and KV cache hit-rate assumptions (owner: Mina). Estimated runtime: 48 hours after receiving traces.
- For the baseline SLOs you described, initial recommendation is 4 dedicated gpus (A100-equivalent) for steady-state 350 rps with autoscale to 9 GPUs for peaks, assuming a quantized 7B and persistent KV cache with 70% hit rate. We'll model scenarios for 13B as an alternate.

Proposed canary plan (high level)
- Week 0: Deploy quantized 7B behind internal route with 5% traffic canary (duration: 24h)
- Evaluate: latency p95/p99, token cost delta, and semantic accuracy on 200 labeled prompts
- Roll forward to 25% / 50% then full if no regressions; automatic fallback to hosted stable model on error budget breach.

Next internal step: Mina will kick off the replay/sizing; Karthik will draft initial topology sketch that includes KV cache placement and network egress optimization. We'll share both results in the Jan 4 packet.

Diego (copied) — please confirm you are comfortable with the 4 -> 9 GPU scaling assumption; we can tighten after the replay results.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery call

Folks — adding a few technical notes from the infra/topology perspective that will go into the Jan 4 packet. High-level guidance and tunables: 

1) KV cache sizing: assume per-session average KV footprint of 80KB. For 10k concurrent sessions (headroom for spikes) that's ~800MB — keep the working set on NVMe + a small in-memory LRU for hottest keys.
2) Batching strategy: continuous batching window of 6–8ms gives good tradeoff on A100-equivalent nodes; with quantized 7B we expect ~22 tokens/sec/node sustained for generator workloads (short-context).
3) Network topology: recommend dedicating at least 2 subnets for inference nodes (one for public egress to hosted fallback, one internal-only); use route policies tied to metric (queue length + p95) for automated failover.
4) Canary metrics: aside from p95/p99, measure token cost delta, generation quality (human-verified set of 200 prompts), and error budget consumption in minutes. Set rollback threshold: p99 > 800ms or quality regression > 2%.

I'll produce a diagram with pod-to-gpu ratios and expected RPS per GPU by 2028-01-04. If they want an aggressive cost-optimized plan, we can sketch a hybrid where small requests hit quantized 7B local nodes and very long-context requests go to a larger instance in-hosted pool.

Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
